title: Luca Guadagnino Says His American Psycho Adaptation Is Not Moving Forward
excerpt:
The director says his planned new adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis's novel is not proceeding.
He praised Scott Z. Burns's screenplay but offered no explanation for the setback.
body_md:
Luca Guadagnino has confirmed on Deadline's Crew Call podcast that his planned new adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis's American Psycho is not moving forward at present. The filmmaker praised the screenplay written by Scott Z. Burns while acknowledging that the project is no longer proceeding.

Lionsgate announced the project in October 2024, with Frenesy Films attached to produce. It was presented as a fresh interpretation of Ellis's novel, not a scene-for-scene remake of Mary Harron's 2000 film. Guadagnino did not identify the reason for the setback, and Lionsgate had not provided a response when the report appeared.

The earlier film starred Christian Bale as Patrick Bateman, an investment banker concealing a murderous double life. Jared Leto, Willem Dafoe, Chloë Sevigny and Reese Witherspoon also appeared. Bale previously offered encouragement to any actor brave enough to tackle the character again.

The director's statement establishes that this particular project is stalled, not that all future adaptations are permanently ruled out. Guadagnino's separate film Artificial, starring Andrew Garfield and dramatizing events surrounding OpenAI and Sam Altman, is scheduled for a December 25, 2026 theatrical release.
